title.narrative: Enhancing Press Freedom and Expression in South Sudan

description.narrative:
To this date, the country is being run on a transitional constitution with insufficient laws and legislations to govern different sectors and operations. This is at the backdrop of challenges of relationships with the Sudan, border issues, security concerns as a result of proliferation of small arms, human rights violations and impunity, poor social infrastructure, high illiteracy rates, diseases and malnutrition and the absence of the rule of law among others.
Exacerbated by its historical and geographical isolation, the period of heightened tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, and internal episodic violence, the legacy of economic underdevelopment and institutional deficits have greatly contributed to the fragility of the country. Just as many South Sudanese were settling to embarked on development, the events leading up to December 2013 conflict saw a new wave of ethnically motivated violence and mass killing across the country especially in the states former Upper Nile, Jonglei and Unity, grossly dissipating the already weak service delivery and human rights in the country. A midst all these crisis, the press freedom and expression is adversely infringed by various state actors within the country. Both citizens and the practicing journalists have come to the realization of a narrowing space for press freedom and expression. These project targets, senior government officials and middle class citizens to get engaged to understand that press freedom and expression are fundamental rights. The project beneficiaries are journalists and the general public that are stakeholders in governance and democratic transformation of South Sudan
